chunks: My father (RA) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-`Attar narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn `Isa, from Ibn Abu Najran, from `Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abu `Abd Allah (AS)

Regarding His Word, the Mighty and High: (Vision comprehends Him not, and He comprehends (all) vision). He said: It is the comprehension of the imagination. Do you not see His Word: (Verily, there have come to you clear proofs from your Lord)? This does not mean the vision of eyes. (Whoever will therefore see, it is for his own soul) does not mean seeing with the eye; and (whoever will be blind, it shall be against himself) does not mean blindness of the eyes. It certainly means comprehension of the imagination, like it is said: so and so has the vision of poetry, so and so has the vision of jurisprudence, so and so has the vision of coins, and so and so has the vision of clothes. Allah is far above visual perception.

key_terms.بَصِيرٌ: Having insight/vision in a specific field

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran mean when it says 'Vision comprehends Him not'?
ai.summary: In al-Tawhid, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) interpreting 'Vision comprehends Him not' (6:103) as a negation of intellectual grasp (ihata al-wahm) rather than physical sight, distinguishing between ocular perception and cognitive understanding. This aligns with the Shia doctrine of tanzih, emphasizing that divine essence transcends sensory limits, while terms like 'basa'ir' and 'ab萨拉' in the Quran often denote spiritual or intellectual insight, as illustrated by the idiomatic use of 'bassir' for expertise in fields like poetry or jurisprudence.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 10. My father (RA) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-`Attar said on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn `Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abu Najran, on the authority of `Abd Allah ibn Sinan that Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS) was asked to interpret the Word of the Mighty and High: Vision comprehends Him not, and He comprehends (all) vision.

He explained: It is the comprehension of the imagination. Do you not see His Word: Verily, there have come to you clear proofs from your Lord. This does not mean the vision of eyes; whoever will therefore see, it is for his own soul. It does not mean seeing with the eye; and whoever will be blind, it shall be against himself.1 This does not mean blindness of the eyes. It certainly means comprehension of the imagination, like it is said: so and so has the vision of poetry, so and so has the vision of jurisprudence, so and so has the vision of coins, and so and so has the vision of clothes. Allah is far above visual perception.
